why: EXP 016's results are published with the three brokers shown as letters, not names. After this record was frozen, the lab recorded each broker's published terms (site/data/provider-terms.json, 2026-10-23). Two of the three brokers have a clause the lab owner has not yet ruled on: one bars use of its trade names without consent, the other bars systematically collecting benchmarks for competitive purposes. The lab owner decided on 2026-10-23 to publish EXP 016's results without saying which broker is which. This amendment changes only how the results are labelled. Nothing measured, counted or decided changes.
timing: Written after the counted run (2026-10-23 08:00:44Z to 08:13:53Z) and before any result was published. The run itself followed the frozen record unchanged.

changes.rule: Each broker is given one of the letters A, B and C by a fixed assignment that is not the order in which the pre-registration lists the brokers. The assignment is kept in the lab's private records and is not published.

changes.what: The published rows leave out what names a broker
changes.rule: The published rows are run.mjs's counted rows with the broker replaced by its letter and four fields reduced: requestedModel and servedProvider are dropped, servedModel is dropped while servedFamily and servedMatches (computed by the frozen lib.mjs) are kept, and the error text is replaced by its class (http-<status>, empty-answer or transport). Every measured value (time, status, tokens, latency, reported cost, finish reason, answer length) is copied unchanged.

changes.what: The frozen analysis scores the published rows
changes.rule: amendment-01/analyse-anon.mjs imports analyse(), spendLedger() and readRuns() from the frozen analyse.mjs unchanged, reads runs-anon/*.jsonl, and gives analyse() the frozen record with its broker list replaced by the letters. Every price, threshold and decision rule is the frozen record's. Its --check mode is the CI recompute.

unchanged: The question, arms, request, changes, replicates, runner, served-model rule, metrics, decision rule, spend and limits are unchanged, and the frozen files stay byte-identical.
limits: The pre-registration was published before the terms were reviewed, and it names the three brokers and each one's model ids. Its calibration also states which broker billed 10% above list. A reader who compares that with the results can probably match at least one letter to a broker. The letters keep the results pages from naming a broker next to a number; they do not make the brokers secret.

Dropping the served model id removes a per-broker detail the record listed as a metric (servedModels per broker). Whether the served model was the requested one is still published for every call, as servedMatches.
notBefore: The results are published only after this amendment is merged to main of odin-labs-ai/odin-rnd.
